title: Hover card content
question: Rows already show name, date, place, fill, and price. What should the hover prove in one glance that the row cannot?

options.label: Ops status board
options.thesis: Lead with booking health: fill remaining, registration deadline urgency, privacy/paused/waitlist flags, page views, and whether a form is attached—skip description prose.
options.viewport: Compact KPI strip + exception chips; no repeated title/media framing when the row already shows them.
options.risk: Feels sparse if an event has no exceptions and a distant deadline.

options.label: Schedule depth
options.thesis: Lead with the timeline the row truncates: end time, registration close, and (for series) the next 3 dates still to come.
options.viewport: Timeline stack first; secondary facts below in a quiet definition list.
options.risk: Less useful mid-week when organisers already know the schedule by heart.

options.label: Mini dossier
options.thesis: Hero image strip + short description + ops facts + flags—more surface area, still one card.
options.viewport: Wider preview with cover band; body mixes prose and facts.
options.risk: Easiest to clutter; fights the List-Not-Preview rule if it starts feeling like a card grid.
